title: overshoot-heuristic-performance-notes-kiara
content:
Goal: quick scratchpad for the "overshoot" heuristic tests. Trying to reproduce persistent tail spikes when a short surge exceeds the autoscale window. Hypothesis: prediction overshoot + cold-KV spill + batching alignment causes transient p99 amplification for ~2–6s after surge onset.

Experiment matrix (short):
- Model: gpt-small-16k-quant (int8 sim); config: kv-cache enabled, small-batch path.
- Hardware: 1xA10G equivalent, 32GB GPU mem, single process.
- Traffic patterns: (A) Poisson base (qps=15) + 2s gaussian microburst to qps=120; (B) stair-step ramp 0->200 qps in 10s; (C) mixed small/large context blend (10% long ctx 4k tokens, rest 64 tokens).
- Policies toggled: autoscale-delay 3s vs 0.5s; spill-to-cold true/false; prefill-on-burst true/false; batch-timeout 6ms/20ms.

Metrics captured: p50/p95/p99 (ms), qps sustained, GPU util (%), KV-cache hit-rate (%), avg tokens/sec. Sampling window 250ms, traces collected at request id granularity.

Quick run summary (not exhaustive):
1) Poisson + 2s microburst (autoscale-delay=3s, spill-to-cold=true, prefill=false, batch-timeout=20ms):
   - baseline (before burst): p50=28ms, p95=92ms, p99=210ms, GPU util=42%, kv-hit=86%
   - during burst (0-2s): p50=72ms, p95=230ms, p99=980ms (big tail), GPU util spikes to 95% then oscillates, kv-hit drops to 44%
   - tail (2-8s after burst): p99 remains ~700–900ms for ~5s then decays: observed repeated KV evictions during spike window.
   - notes: long p99 seems correlated with KV miss storms; spill-to-cold causing disk fetch + batch amplification.

2) Same as (1) but spill-to-cold=false (i.e., keep in-GPU queue, drop if necessary):
   - during burst: p99=360ms (much improved), p95=180ms, GPU util capped 88%
   - kv-hit stays ~82% (no eviction churn)
   - tradeoff: some requests dropped/queued longer but fewer severe tails.

3) Stair-step ramp (0->200 qps in 10s) with prefill-on-burst=true and batch-timeout=6ms:
   - warmup smoother, p99 peaks around 420ms then stabilizes to 260ms as batches adapt, GPU util ramps monotonically to 88%
   - prefill reduced initial KV-miss by ~22% (instrumentation: priming requests touched model segment earlier)

4) Mixed context (10% long ctx) with small batch-timeout:
   - long ctx requests cause multipliers: single long request stalls KV locality leading to short-ctx being queued behind large decode; p95 for short ctx jumps from 95ms->310ms when a long ctx enters a batch.
   - mitigation: small-priority-lane for short ctx reduced p95 back to ~110ms at cost of 3% throughput loss.

Hypothesis refinement:
- Overshoot occurs when the autoscaler (or dispatch layer) opens capacity too slowly and the runtime tries to 'bunch' many inflight requests into a few large batches. If some batches contain long-context decodes or missing KV pages, they become stragglers and amplify tail.
- KV eviction churn is a major amplifier: when KV eviction is enabled + memory pressure + sudden burst, the system does small async fetches causing many small stalls that serialize on the hotpath.
- Batch-timeout tuning (lower ms) helps but increases unit cost; prefill (speculative priming) helps reduce misses without increasing batch sizes too much.

Actionable next tests (brief):
- A: Run microburst with KV eviction capped: limit evictions per-second and measure p99.
- B: Test prefill with aggressive priority lanes: prefill only for top-10% frequent tenants and observe tail improvement.
- C: Run long-ctx isolation experiment where long ctx are routed to a dedicated lane (no co-batching). Measure cross-impact.
- D: Try autoscale-delay of 0.5s + faster warmup kernel selection to see if early capacity reduces bunching.

Notes / heuristics to try in runtime:
- If qps spike > 4x baseline and kv-hit drops > 20% in 500ms, temporarily: (1) reduce batch-timeout to 6ms, (2) enable short-priority lane, (3) disable in-flight KV eviction for 4s. Evaluate tail improvement.
- Consider a 'burst-prefill' mode that sends a small set of speculative short priming requests (2–4) when surge detection triggers to warm KV pages.

Telemetry & quick visuals (hand notes):
- ASCII heatmap (simplified): time across top, latency colors approximated by ranges. During burst see bright red band (p99) for ~5s post-burst.
- Correlated traces show spikes aligning with KV-fetch latency (~15–40ms each) stacking when many misses occur.

Open questions / random observations:
- Does kernel selection latency (compilation/cold kernels) contribute? Observed small ~12ms jitter for first few batches after cold-start of a variant. Add compile-metrics to traces.
- Multi-tenant vs single-tenant: these runs were single-tenant. Multi-tenant could magnify eviction churn—need to rerun.
- Could model-quantization (int8) interaction with batch packing cause longer decode peaks? Some decode loops slower for int8 on this kernel path.

Quick raw numbers snapshot (run A):
- burst amplitude: 15->120 qps, burst duration 2.1s
- p50/p95/p99 baseline: 28/92/210 ms
- p50/p95/p99 during burst: 72/230/~980 ms
- kv-hit baseline/during: 86% -> 44%

Todo (short):
- [ ] schedule eviction-cap test (A). assign: Ravi. due: 2025-02-18.
- [ ] build small-priority-lane PoC in runtime: assign: Kiara; PR draft referenced above.
- [ ] instrument kernel-compile-latency and include in trace logs.

References / links inside org: JIRA-RT-4123 (tail spikes), PR #879 runtime change (speculative prefill), confluence: /runtimes/burst-mitigation (draft).

End notes: quick scratchpad. Will convert to structured experiment doc if A/B looks promising. Keep this raw as lab notebook.
